identity_reason: a layout primitive only places other components and has no look of its own to derive
concept: Stack lines up units and parts on the 4px step, so the gaps between appliances on a screen follow the same rhythm as the holes and insets inside them.

root.why: A stack keeps its children in fixed positions so a layout never reflows between states.

column.why: Units stack top to bottom on a phone, each keeping its own face and its place in the order.

row.why: Parts sit side by side in one row, like keys printed along the bottom of a case.

g-xs.why: The smallest gap is one 4px step, the same pitch the grille holes sit on.

g-sm.why: A small gap of two steps separates a label from the part it names.

g-md.why: A medium gap of four steps separates neighbouring parts inside one unit face.

g-lg.why: A large gap of six steps separates one unit from the next so each reads as its own appliance.

g-xl.why: The section gap of eight steps separates groups of units, such as rooms on a home screen.

a-start.why: Start alignment keeps labels on the inset line where printing sits on a case.

a-center.why: Centre alignment puts the loud control in the clear area the hand expects to find it in.

a-end.why: End alignment places the lowercase model name on the bottom right inset line.

a-stretch.why: Stretch lets a display window run the full inner width of the unit, aligned to the inset.
